profile.campus: Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico (Meta's Los Lunas data center campus; Data Center Dynamics reported seven buildings on the campus as of 2023, with a further two-building expansion announced)
profile.address: 4250, Messenger Loop Northwest, Meta Los Lunas Data Center, Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico, 87031
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures on Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico, on Messenger Loop Northwest in the Albuquerque metropolitan area. Meta selected Los Lunas for its first New Mexico data center and broke ground on an initial building in 2016. Meta's own current fact sheet for the site states the campus has drawn more than two and a half billion dollars of investment and that the facility came online in 2018 after that initial construction phase, and the campus has expanded across multiple additional buildings since. Data Center Dynamics, covering the campus's 2023 expansion, reported seven buildings standing at that point with a further two building, roughly eight hundred million dollar expansion then under construction, a project subsequent local reporting identified as Buildings 7 and 8 and described as the first in Meta's global portfolio purpose built for AI and machine learning workloads rather than general web infrastructure. The Village of Los Lunas approved that expansion in a vote that drew public debate over water use, discussed further below. Meta does not publish a current, confirmed building count, per building square footage, or a campus wide total square footage figure. One third party real estate and investment analysis, not verified here against a primary source, put the built campus at eight buildings and roughly 3.8 million square feet by late 2025, and described individual data halls as drawing on the order of 40 megawatts each with headroom to roughly 80 megawatts. This entry treats those specific figures as unconfirmed rather than established fact, consistent with the rule that a power figure is only recorded here when a primary source explicitly labels it for a specific building, which has not happened for Los Lunas.

Los Lunas won this investment for reasons common to New Mexico's pursuit of large industrial projects, chiefly available land on a flat mesa outside Albuquerque, access to Public Service Company of New Mexico's transmission grid, and New Mexico's long standing use of industrial revenue bonds, IRBs, to give large projects favorable property and gross receipts tax treatment without the village itself issuing debt. Village records and contemporaneous news coverage describe the Los Lunas council approving IRB authorizations for Meta's Greater Kudu LLC affiliate on more than one occasion, including an initial 2016 authorization and further authorizations tied to later expansion phases, with press accounts describing nominal bond ceilings in the tens of billions of dollars, a structure typical of New Mexico IRB deals in which the authorized bond capacity is a legal ceiling for tax purposes rather than a reflection of actual capital spent. This registry has not independently reviewed the underlying Village resolutions and treats the widely reported dollar figures as press accounts pending direct document review, not as verified bond totals.

Power for the campus is supplied by Public Service Company of New Mexico, PNM. Policy researchers tracking New Mexico data center growth describe Meta's arrangement as a special services contract paired with a voluntary renewable energy rate, and describe this Los Lunas campus as the longest running large scale data center load in the state, a status that has made it a reference point in New Mexico's regulatory response to rising data center demand, including Public Regulation Commission investigatory docket 24-00257-UT on large load interconnection and 2025 state legislation, Senate Bills 169 and 170 and House Bill 93, addressing data center site readiness and microgrid rules. Among generation sources named specifically in connection with this campus, PNM and Meta marked commercial operation in July 2022 of the Route 66 Solar Facility, a 49.5 megawatt, more than 450 acre solar installation in neighboring Cibola County built by NextEra Energy Resources with more than 150,000 bifacial modules and built specifically to help supply renewable power to the Los Lunas data center. In June 2025 Meta and XGS Energy announced a 150 megawatt advanced geothermal project for New Mexico, to be delivered through the PNM grid in two phases with full output targeted for 2030 and described by the companies as generating power without consuming water, though the state's own announcement described the project as serving Meta's New Mexico data center operations generally rather than naming this campus by name. Meta's broader fact sheet reports the company supporting 21 renewable energy projects across nine New Mexico counties, adding 1,465 megawatts of new renewable generation capacity and 488 megawatts of battery storage, a statewide figure not broken out by project or allocated to any single campus. No source reviewed for this entry documents standby diesel generation capacity or confirmed on site, behind the meter generation for this campus. In keeping with that gap in the record, this entry does not assign a megawatt figure for IT capacity, utility interconnection capacity, standby generation, or on site generation to this specific building, since Meta has not published a building level figure for any of the four.

Water use at this campus has drawn sustained public attention in a high desert region where agricultural water rights are already contested. Meta's own sustainability materials commit the company to being water positive globally by 2030, describe cooling technology at its data centers as more water efficient than industry standard designs, describe reusing water before discharge, and describe native landscaping intended to reduce irrigation needs. Local reporting in 2021, as the Village considered the roughly 800 million dollar expansion described above, documented organized resident opposition under the name Valencia Water Watchers, more than 200 signed petitions asking the council to delay its vote, and public comments from area farmers describing irrigation water curtailments on their own operations amid a Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District irrigation season that had been cut short the year before for water supply reasons. Trade press coverage from that period put Facebook's reported regional water withdrawal at approximately 59 million gallons in 2020 against a company claim of having restored approximately 64 million gallons to the Rio Grande watershed that same year, a restoration claim a separate third party analysis also cited when describing Meta's broader pledge to restore more than twice its annual water consumption to local watersheds. That same unverified third party analysis described a Village of Los Lunas water allocation to Meta on the order of 1.5 million gallons per day, expandable toward 4.5 million gallons per day at full campus buildout, and cited a 2023 consumption figure of roughly 75 million gallons for the year. This registry has not confirmed those specific allocation and consumption figures against Village records or a Meta disclosure and reports them here only as attributed, unverified secondary reporting, offered because it is the kind of local record detail worth flagging even where it cannot be independently confirmed.

What remains unknown from the public record includes the precise current building count and any confirmed per building square footage, the exact terms and resolution numbers behind each IRB authorization and any payment in lieu of taxes or gross receipts tax arrangement, verified current water allocation and consumption figures, and any building specific IT capacity, utility interconnection capacity, standby generation, or on site generation figure.

In this registry's own mapped coordinates, this building carries the OpenStreetMap unit tag D, and sits at the eastern end of a second, southern row of two buildings, roughly a quarter mile south of the A, B, C row. OpenStreetMap's ref tag lists this building as ref 4, the same ref value carried by the other southern building, unit E, osm:way/1548035623. This registry has not been able to determine from public sources which building, if either, corresponds to any Meta internal building number 4, and neither building is arbitrarily assigned a different number here to manufacture a false distinction. Beyond that positional and tagging metadata, no primary or press source reviewed for this entry distinguishes this specific building from its siblings by function, capacity, or completion date, and no such distinction is invented here.

profile.regional_context: Valencia County sits in the Albuquerque metro area along the historic Route 66 corridor, for which the Meta-linked Cibola County solar facility is named. New Mexico's data center growth has drawn on the state's high solar-resource potential and PNM's renewable-energy procurement, and Los Lunas has used industrial revenue bond financing repeatedly to support Meta's expansions, per Data Center Dynamics reporting on the village's approvals.
profile.campus_power_note: Campus wide power note, not specific to any one building. Meta does not publish IT capacity, utility interconnection capacity, standby generation, or on site generation megawatt figures for the Los Lunas campus, whether broken out by building or as a campus wide total. Meta's company wide fact sheet reports supporting 21 renewable energy projects across 9 New Mexico counties, adding 1,465 megawatts of new renewable generation capacity and 488 megawatts of battery storage statewide, a total not allocated to any single campus. Generation named specifically in connection with this campus includes the 49.5 megawatt Route 66 Solar Facility in Cibola County, built by NextEra Energy Resources, which PNM and Meta marked as reaching commercial operation in July 2022. In June 2025 Meta and XGS Energy announced a 150 megawatt advanced geothermal project for New Mexico, to be delivered through the PNM grid in two phases with full output targeted for 2030, described by the companies and the state as serving Meta's New Mexico data center operations generally rather than named to this campus specifically. Meta procures power here from Public Service Company of New Mexico under what policy researchers describe as a special services contract with a voluntary renewable energy rate, and that same research describes this campus as the longest running large scale data center load in New Mexico, now a reference point in New Mexico Public Regulation Commission docket 24-00257-UT on large load interconnection and in 2025 legislation, Senate Bills 169 and 170 and House Bill 93. No standby diesel generation capacity or confirmed on site, behind the meter generation for this campus has been documented in the sources reviewed. One unverified third party real estate and investment analysis estimated roughly 40 megawatts of draw per data hall with headroom to about 80 megawatts, and reported a dedicated PNM substation commissioned in November 2024. Those figures are not confirmed against a primary source and are not treated as established fact in this registry.
profile.campus_buildings_total: At least 7 buildings completed as of Data Center Dynamics 2023 reporting, plus a 2 building, roughly 800 million dollar AI dedicated expansion, reported locally as Buildings 7 and 8, approved by the Village of Los Lunas and under construction as of early 2025. Meta does not publish a current, confirmed total. One unverified third party real estate and investment analysis put the built count at 8 buildings by late 2025.

reading.body:
Meta's Los Lunas campus is a multi-building installation in Valencia County, south of Albuquerque, that began commercial operation in 2016 and has expanded to seven buildings as of 2023 with a two-building, roughly $800 million expansion announced and under construction. Meta does not publish the total megawatts of IT capacity, square footage, or per-building figures for this site. The campus is the only data center facility in New Mexico with a published power specification on this site, though that specification itself remains undisclosed.

Power supply to Los Lunas is the operative constraint to watch. Meta and PNM marked commercial operation of the Route 66 Solar Facility in July 2022, a 49.5-megawatt solar installation built specifically to supply this campus. Meta's broader New Mexico commitment totals 885 megawatts of new renewable energy and 100 megawatts of battery storage, framed as supporting both current products and future AI hardware generations at Los Lunas. Whether this renewable capacity and the state's solar resource can scale further with the announced expansion, or whether additional grid infrastructure is required, is not published.

The financial and political commitment is substantial. Meta has invested more than $2.5 billion in the New Mexico campus overall and the Village of Los Lunas has approved industrial revenue bonds to support successive expansion phases. The campus is designed to reach roughly 400 operational jobs once complete. The scale of this build-out and its multi-year expansion timeline place Los Lunas among the material data center projects now being constructed for AI workloads, but its unpublished power capacity leaves its rank in the national AI infrastructure landscape opaque.
